name: Long wool scarf
description: A very long navy knitted scarf with two cream stripes and a fringe at each end. Worn loosely over the mouth and nose, it keeps out the cold, and there is enough of it left to wrap the head as well.
notes: Folded in four, 270 mm by 224 mm and 52 mm tall with its fringe: `cloth-navy` knit with rib lines, two `cloth-cream` stripes across the top fold. Slot `face`, as the cowl and bandanas over the face take. Wearing it as a headwrap is the draft `long_wool_scarf_head_wrap` on the same model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Long wool scarf (head wrap)
description: A very long navy knitted scarf wrapped round the head as well as the face, warm enough for a hard frost.
notes: The same scarf as `long_wool_scarf`, worn wrapped over the head and mouth, so it rides on the `long_wool_scarf` model: off the body both look the same folded scarf. Slot `hood`, as headscarves take; it covers the face too, which one slot cannot express. Switching between the two ways of wearing it needs a wear-mode action in Deadvox, not authored here. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Wool scarf
description: A plain grey knitted scarf with a short fringe. Wound over the mouth and nose, it takes the bite out of cold air.
notes: Folded in three, 200 mm by 184 mm and 38 mm tall with its fringe: `wool-grey` knit with `plastic-charcoal` rib lines. Slot `face`, as for the long scarf. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Prayer shawl
description: A large cream wool shawl banded in black near each end, with a woven silver neckband and knotted white fringes at its corners. It is worn over the shoulders and wraps the upper body.
notes: Folded square, 378 mm by 330 mm with its fringes and 36 mm tall: `cloth-cream` wool, three `cloth-black` bands near each end, a `cloth-shimmer` neckband along the back, two knotted `cloth-bright-white` fringes at the front corners, each a knot, a cord over the edge and six thin strands fanning out on the floor (the other two lie under the fold). Slot `cloak`, as wraps worn over everything take. The box counts the fringes fanning out past the fold. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Nylon throat guard
description: A padded black nylon collar with a rounded bib over the throat, closed at the back with a hook-and-loop tab. Made for hockey, it stops a skate blade or a slash across the neck.
notes: Standing on its edge, 134 mm across and 86 mm tall: a padded `nylon-black` band open at the back, the bib dropping 45 mm at the front, `cloth-charcoal` binding, `hook-loop-grey` tabs at the opening. Slot `neck`, as collars take; one slot means a necklace and a throat guard cannot be worn together (a separate `throat` slot would fix that, proposed in the report). The open collar's box includes the neck hole. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

description: A padded khaki canvas collar with a rounded bib over the throat, closed at the back with a hook-and-loop tab. It guards the neck in rough sports.
notes: Rides on the `throat_guard` model, recoloured: khaki canvas with brown binding. Slot `neck`, as collars take; one slot means a necklace and a throat guard cannot be worn together (a separate `throat` slot would fix that, proposed in the report). notes: Rides on the `throat_guard` model, recoloured: `aramid-gold` with `webbing-black` binding. Slot `neck`, as collars take; one slot means a necklace and a throat guard cannot be worn together (a separate `throat` slot would fix that, proposed in the report). name: Ballistic throat guard
description: A thick ballistic collar in a coyote nylon cover with a nylon throat guard sewn inside it, the front flap dropping over the throat. Taken off a body armour vest and made to be worn alone.
notes: Standing on its edge, 176 mm across and 112 mm tall: a 14 mm `nylon-coyote` ballistic collar open at the back, its throat flap dropping 52 mm with a `hook-loop-grey` patch, the `nylon-black` inner guard showing above the top edge, hook-and-loop tabs at the opening. Slot `neck`, as collars take; one slot means a necklace and a throat guard cannot be worn together (a separate `throat` slot would fix that, proposed in the report). The open collar's box includes the neck hole. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Fencing gorget
description: A stiff collar of thick rubber under black nylon, flaring at the front into a broad bib over the collarbones, bound in red. Sword fencers wear it against thrusts to the throat; the back of the neck is barely covered.
notes: Standing on its lower edge, 280 mm across and 172 mm tall: a `nylon-black` collar open at the back, a bib sloping smoothly down from the collar over the front, flaps over the sides of the nape reaching round to meet the bib, `cloth-red` binding and a `hook-loop-grey` closure. The shell is thick rubber under nylon, so the model shows only the nylon cover. Slot `neck`, as collars take; one slot means a necklace and a throat guard cannot be worn together (a separate `throat` slot would fix that, proposed in the report). The open collar's box includes the neck hole. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.
